postings.description:
Note: Partly is headquartered in Austin, TX with offices in London, UK, Christchurch, NZ and Auckland, NZ. Wherever you're based, we'll connect you with your nearest office for onboarding, and fly you to join the full team for our quarterly "Season Openers" (we cover travel and accommodation). If you're relocating to join us, we can also assist with relocation costs.



🚀 OUR STORY

Partly is building the infrastructure for anyone to repair anything. We believe everything built should be repairable, and we're building frontier AI to put repair knowledge to work, starting with the $2tn automotive market.

Our model, Interpreter, is the first AI purpose-built to understand repair. Trained on 1M+ car models and 1B+ parts, it reads a repair job the way an estimator does, resolves damage into the exact purchasable part, and shows its reasoning with a confidence score. On real production jobs, an estimator working with Interpreter reaches 98.8% parts-list accuracy, against 92.1% with today's tools. It powers PartlyRepair, used by collision shops, workshops and suppliers to take the admin off the job; PartlyLabs, the agentic infrastructure enterprises use to deploy Interpreter across their own workflows; and a developer API.

Founded by ex-Rocket Lab engineers, we've raised a $50m Series B led by DST Global (Anthropic, Airbnb, Meta, TikTok, Spotify), with Blackbird Ventures, WNDR, Activant Capital, Icehouse Ventures, Square Peg, Airtree and Ecliptic Venture Capital. Hear it from the team: Why Partly exists https://www.partly.com/nz/careers/videos/why-partly-exists and AI at Partly https://www.partly.com/nz/careers/videos/ai-at-partly.

We're always keen to meet talented people who want to help connect the world's parts.

If you don't see a role that fits but think you'd be a great addition to the team, get in touch and tell us how you could contribute.

 - Excellent communication and collaboration skills, enabling effective engagement with cross-functional teams and external stakeholders.

 - Ability to prioritise tasks, manage multiple projects simultaneously, and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

 - A passion for data accuracy, integrity, and continuous improvement, with a commitment to maintaining high standards of parts data quality.

🖍️ THIS ROLE

Partly is building the AI infrastructure layer for the global automotive parts industry. At the core of that infrastructure is Partly Rails - the transactional backbone that orchestrates the full job lifecycle, from estimation through procurement, reconciliation, and close. It is the layer everything else runs on.

As Principal or Staff PM for Infrastructure APIs & Developer Ecosystem, you own the product that makes Partly's infrastructure accessible to the world. That means owning Rails as an end-to-end transactional product in its own right, building the external API program that lets customers and third-party systems integrate with confidence, and growing the developer ecosystem that compounds Partly's reach across markets without requiring direct Partly involvement in every integration.

This is a platform product role with two connected mandates: keeping the core job flow principled, auditable, and scalable; and building the external developer program - portal, documentation, partner ecosystem, and agentic API evolution - that turns Partly's infrastructure into a platform others build on.

You'll be operating at an inflection point. AI-assisted development and agents are compressing product discovery and delivery cycles. The best PMs we know are no longer waiting for engineering capacity to test an idea - they're building rapid prototypes themselves, deploying them, reading the signal, and deciding within days. We're looking for someone already working that way, or actively building toward it.




💻 WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - Partly Rails. The end-to-end transactional job flow - from job creation through estimation, procurement, reconciliation, and close. You own this as a product: opinionated in design, reliable at scale, and compelling as a value proposition for any system that runs on it. Key metrics: API feature coverage of the job flow, jobs processed on Rails APIs, uptime, latency, error rates.

 - External Integration APIs. The full external API program - API governance, versioning policy, and the standards that define how the outside world connects to Partly. Key metrics: API adoption rate, integration depth, versioning health.

 - Developer Portal & Experience. The developer platform - documentation, tooling, sandbox environments, and everything a third-party integrator needs to go from first call to production. Key metrics: time to first test job, time to first production job, developer satisfaction.

 - Developer Ecosystem. The global network of integration partners building on Partly's infrastructure - identifying them, activating them, and creating the conditions for the ecosystem to grow. Key metrics: active external integrations, ecosystem growth rate, partner retention.

 - Agentic API Evolution. As AI agents become a new class of API consumer alongside traditional system integrations, you own evolving Partly's API offer to serve them - designing for autonomous, context-aware, and reliable agentic usage patterns. Key metrics: agentic integration adoption, reliability under autonomous consumption.




💻 WHAT YOU'LL DO

Own your product, end-to-end

 - Define and evolve the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for Partly's infrastructure and developer platform.

 - Own the metrics that reflect the health of the Rails transaction layer and the growth of the developer ecosystem - and use them to steer all decisions.

 - Lead go-to-market alignment for API releases, ecosystem programs, and integration partnerships.

 - Act as the single accountable owner - for successes, failures, and everything in between.

Stay close to customers

 - Maintain direct, regular contact with integration partners and developers - not as an escalation path, but as a core weekly input to prioritisation.

 - Understand the difference between what developers ask for and what they actually need to ship successfully.

 - Combine qualitative developer feedback with API usage data, integration telemetry, and support signals - and reconcile them.

Build and ship, not just specify

 - Prototype API experiences, documentation flows, and developer tooling yourself using AI-assisted development - fast and disposable.

 - Treat the prototype as the hypothesis. Test with real integrators before writing the spec.

 - Work hands-on with data: define metrics, build dashboards, query logs, read the signals directly.

Lead in the human loop

 - Partner closely with engineering leads to balance platform capability, developer experience, and technical sustainability.

 - Align partner success, GTM, and support teams around the ecosystem strategy.

 - Communicate API roadmap and deprecation decisions clearly and early - external developers depend on stability and deserve advance notice.

Lead in the agent loop

 - Design APIs and instrumentation with agentic consumption in mind - not as a future consideration, but as a present design constraint.

 - Define what "working" means for agent-consumed APIs: reliability, observability, graceful failure, and context fidelity.

 - Think in systems: how does a change to the API surface propagate through every integration downstream?

Raise the bar

 - Set the standard for API design, documentation quality, and developer experience across Partly.

 - Help define what an excellent external developer program looks like as the ecosystem scales.




🥷 WHAT YOU BRING

Non-negotiables

 - Proven experience owning developer-facing API products: API design, versioning, governance, and lifecycle management.

 - Practical experience building or scaling a developer ecosystem - partner programs, integration networks, or developer communities.

 - Deep understanding of developer experience as a product discipline: what good onboarding, documentation, and tooling actually look like at each stage of maturity.

 - Commercial and technical depth - you can engage credibly with engineers on API architecture and translate developer needs into clear business outcomes.

 - 5+ years owning platform or infrastructure products with clear accountability for adoption metrics, not just delivery.

 - You build rapid prototypes yourself - with AI-assisted tools, LLM-assisted development, or code - as a first instinct for testing ideas.

 - Strong analytical instinct: you define the metrics, build the view, read the data, and act on it - without waiting for a data team to hand it to you.

Strong signals we look for

 - Experience designing APIs for agentic or LLM-based consumption, beyond traditional system integrations.

 - Familiarity with transactional or workflow APIs in domains such as payments, logistics, supply chain, or insurance.

 - Experience running a partner or ISV program at scale.

 - Comfort owning reliability, observability, and non-functional requirements as first-class product concerns.

 - Founder background, or early employee at a platform-first startup that scaled materially.

 - You've killed or radically changed something you personally believed in, and can explain why.

Bonus

 - Domain knowledge in automotive aftermarket, collision repair, or insurance claims.

 - Experience scaling developer platforms across multiple geographies.

 - Experience with product-led growth motions applied to a developer or API product.

 - Experience building or operating products with meaningful agentic or automation components.




🧭 HOW YOU'LL THINK AND OPERATE

We're not looking for framework experts or consensus-drivers. We're looking for someone who thinks like this:

 - "I shipped a sandbox version of the new flow yesterday. Two integration partners have already tried it. Here's what they got stuck on."

 - "The p99 latency spike on job creation is the highest-priority issue this week — not the feature request in the backlog."

 - "Here's what the integration telemetry shows. Here's what I think it means. Here's what I'm changing. Here's when I'll know if I'm wrong."

 - "An agent just tried to consume this API autonomously and failed in a way we didn't design for. That's the most interesting problem we have right now."

Speed, ownership, and judgment are the baseline. What differentiates the best candidates is the ability to operate fluently across both the developer-facing surface - documentation, DX, partner programs - and the infrastructure layer beneath it, and to shrink the distance between intent and outcome.

🖍️ THIS ROLE

Insurers and work providers pay for the repair and set the rules it runs by. This role owns Partly's entire product relationship with them.

Partly creates value for insurers through three layers, and you own how all three land for this customer. Interpreter, our domain-specific AI foundation model, turns damage and estimate data into an accurate, complete parts picture early in the claim. Rails, our API layer, lets insurers and the systems they already run integrate directly with Partly's job processing infrastructure. And our agentic, highly automated user-level capabilities progressively absorb work that is manual across the industry today. Together these move the metrics an insurer is measured on: total cost of risk, cycle times, customer satisfaction, total loss rate and operational efficiency across the claims organisation.

You build for several distinct personas inside the insurer's workflow, each needing a different product on the same foundation: appraisers reviewing parts decisions and authorising spend; claims handlers and adjusters running the file; dispute and escalation teams revisiting jobs long after they close; network managers allocating work; and the parts, procurement and sustainability leads who set policy in the first place. You are the single accountable person for the value insurers get from Partly, and for what that unlocks across the rest of the network.

The remit is global, covering New Zealand, the UK and the US, with a strong first focus on the US, where you will be based. Claims structures, parts policy and competitive incumbents differ sharply across the three, so deciding what is genuinely one global product and what has to stay local is yours to call.

This is an enterprise product with a consumer-grade bar. You will be in the room before contracts exist, shaping pilots and building the artefacts that prove value, then making sure that same product expands and retains itself once the relationship is live.

The core challenge is trust at institutional scale. Automation advances only as fast as an insurer's confidence in it, so owning that trajectory, and the evidence and audit trail that makes each step defensible to a claims director, is the heart of the role.

You'll be operating at an inflection point. AI-assisted development is compressing discovery and delivery: the best PMs we know build rapid prototypes themselves, deploy them, read the signal and decide within days. We want someone already working that way, or building toward it.



💻 WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - The Insurer Experience, End-to-End. The full product experience for every insurer-side user across all markets: appraisers, claims handlers and adjusters, dispute and escalation teams, network managers, and parts, procurement and sustainability leads. Key metrics: NPS, time-to-value, appraiser time per claim, task completion rate, support contact rate.

 - Insurer Rules and Compliance. Definition, administration and evolution of per-insurer parts rules, supplier waterfalls, thresholds and evidence requirements, codified in the product rather than administered by hand. Key metrics: rule compliance rate, appraiser approval rate, share of rules codified, time to configure a new insurer, per-job insurer attribution accuracy.

 - Verification and Audit. Automating the manual claim verification insurer engineers perform today, and extending it into the value band nobody currently checks. Key metrics: share of claims verified without manual review, verification turnaround, engineer hours displaced, value recovered per verified claim.

 - Insurer Intelligence and Reporting. The portfolio-level view of what an insurer's network actually bought, what was available at the moment of order, and how that performs across sites and over time, including the consent and permission model that makes named reporting legitimate. Key metrics: reporting adoption, availability-versus-uptake coverage, consent coverage, dispute rate and resolution time.

 - Enterprise Product-Led Growth. The full insurer arc from pre-sales pilot through onboarding, activation, cohort expansion and network-wide mandate, treated as product design and instrumentation problems. Key metrics: pilot-to-contract conversion, time to first mandated cohort, cohort-to-network expansion, insurer seat and site expansion, net revenue retention.

 - Automation and the Agentic Experience. The strategy for moving insurers from checking every job to supervising exceptions, including where the human stays in the loop, how delegated authority is earned, and how control is preserved as more runs autonomously. Key metrics: automation rate by workflow stage, share of stages completed via delegation, supervision and intervention rate, override frequency, delegated authority thresholds.

 - Integration Experience. How Partly fits into the estimating platforms, claims systems and appraisal platforms insurers already run. A poor integration experience is a poor Partly experience, and it matters more, not less, as agents need clean context across systems. Key metrics: integration reliability, cross-system task completion rate, insurer-reported friction.
   


💻 WHAT YOU'LL DO

Own your product, end-to-end

 - Define and evolve the product vision, strategy and roadmap for insurer products globally, aligned with company direction and the wider platform.

 - Continuously assess and improve Product-Market Fit across markets with materially different claims structures, parts policies and competitive incumbents.

 - Decide deliberately what is global and what is local, and defend that line when a single account pushes on it.

 - Own key product, growth and commercial metrics and use them to steer every decision.

 - Act as the single accountable owner, for successes, failures and everything in between.

Stay close to customers

 - Maintain direct, regular contact with appraisers, claims handlers and insurer decision-makers. This is a core weekly activity, not an occasional input.

 - Sit with appraisers while they work a queue. Understand what they check, what they cannot see, and what would let them stop checking.

 - Map the insurer's actual internal process, not the one on the org chart, and design against where the decision and the money really sit.

 - Combine qualitative insight with quantitative usage and outcome data, and reconcile the two when they disagree.

Be in the room before the contract is

 - Partner with Sales on enterprise pipelines: shape the pilot, build the artefacts that convert, and take the hard questions yourself.

 - Design pilots that prove a mechanism rather than produce a flattering number, and hold the line on what the evidence actually supports.

 - Turn what you learn in pre-sales directly into roadmap, and tell Sales plainly when the answer is no.

Build and ship, not just specify

 - Prototype new product iterations yourself using AI-assisted development and LLM-assisted tooling: fast, disposable, real. We call this vibe coding; it is our default mode for product discovery.

 - Treat the prototype as the hypothesis. Put it in front of a real appraiser before writing the spec.

 - Work hands-on with data: define metrics, build dashboards, query the warehouse, read the signals directly.

 - Know the difference between a causal claim and a selection effect, and design the measurement that separates them.

Lead in the human loop

 - Partner closely with engineering leads to balance discovery, delivery and technical sustainability.

 - Align GTM, Customer Success, operations and support across three regions around one product direction.

 - Communicate priorities and reasoning clearly, especially when the answer is no.

 - Represent the insurer's reality in every internal decision, as evidence rather than as a summary.

Lead in the agent loop

 - Design and instrument feedback loops that let you learn from system behaviour alongside user behaviour.

 - Define what working means for agentic and AI-driven features, in terms of evals, edge-case handling and observable outcomes.

 - Own the trust trajectory: design how insurers move from checking everything to supervising exceptions, without ever losing the audit trail that makes it defensible.

 - Think in systems: how does a decision on the insurer side change repairer and supplier behaviour across the whole network?

Raise the bar

 - Contribute beyond your product boundary: cross-product coherence, shared principles and the overall product craft at Partly.

 - Help define what excellent product ownership looks like here as the team grows.
   


🥷 WHAT YOU BRING

Non-negotiables

 - Genuine customer obsession, with a demonstrated habit of spending time with users in their actual work context and a track record of that depth driving product direction.

 - 5+ years owning complex, enterprise B2B software products end-to-end, with clear accountability for outcomes rather than delivery. Multi-persona, operational or workflow-heavy domains preferred.

 - A strong personal track record in pre-sales engagement for enterprise pipelines: shaping pilots, building what converts, and carrying what you learn back into the roadmap.

 - Proficiency with corporate process and process modelling. You can map how a large organisation really works and design product against it.

 - A clear point of view on agentic product design: how an experience migrates from manual operation to supervised delegation, and how automation earns institutional trust progressively.

 - Demonstrated PLG instincts inside an enterprise motion: onboarding, activation, expansion and retention as product design problems, with personal accountability for the numbers.

 - Experience with API-first or integration-dependent products, and strong intuition for where cross-system friction quietly destroys value.

 - You build rapid prototypes yourself, with AI-assisted tools, LLM-assisted development or code, as a first instinct for testing ideas.

 - Strong analytical instinct: you define the metrics, build the view, read the data and act on it, without waiting for a data team.

 - Excellent judgement in a multi-stakeholder environment where insurer, repairer and supplier interests compete, and where the paying customer is not the daily user.

 - Working understanding of how US collision repair is funded and governed, including DRP and steering dynamics and alternative-parts cost pressure, and the right to work in the US.

Strong signals we look for

 - Hands-on experience shipping AI-assisted or agent-driven workflows in production where the human stays in the loop.

 - Experience in automotive, insurance, claims or equivalent operational verticals involving parts, supply chain or job management.

 - Experience building products carrying compliance, audit or regulatory weight, where the record of what happened is part of the product.

 - Exposure to marketplace or network dynamics from the demand side.

 - Experience running one product across multiple geographies with genuinely different rules and incumbents.

 - Founder background, or early employee at a startup that scaled materially.

 - You've killed or radically changed something you personally believed in, and can explain why.

Bonus

 - Relationships across the US carrier, TPA or claims-technology ecosystem.

 - Familiarity with the estimating and claims platforms insurers run day to day.

 - Experience selling or building against an entrenched incumbent.

 - Experience building or operating products with meaningful agentic or automation components.
   


🧭 HOW YOU'LL THINK AND OPERATE

We're not looking for framework experts or consensus-drivers. We're looking for someone who thinks like this:

 - "I sat with two appraisers this week and watched them work a queue. Here's the one thing they check that we don't show them, and here's what I'm changing."

 - "I built a version of the insurer report this afternoon. Their analyst will attack it on selection, so here's the cut that survives that."

 - "Here's what the data shows. Here's what I think it means. Here's what I'm doing about it. Here's when I'll be wrong."

 - "I own the insurer product. If it's broken, that's on me. Let me tell you exactly how it broke and what I'm doing about it."

Speed, ownership and judgement are the baseline. What differentiates the best candidates is the ability to move fluidly between the claims director's boardroom and the appraiser's screen, and to translate both into a product that holds up under scrutiny.

HTTPS://APP.NOTION.COM/P/PARTLY/US-BENEFITS-3A72CF96686281E6BA36DD840193C3EC



📍 LOCATION

United States - Austin, Texas. This is an in-office role with global product responsibility. New hires spend their first two weeks at HQ in Christchurch and one week per quarter thereafter; travel and accommodation covered. Expect regular travel to NZ and the UK, and to insurer customers across all three markets.


A NOTE ON BAR

We're looking for someone rare. Not rare because of their title or the brands on their CV - rare because of how they think, what they own, and how they operate.

The insurer relationship is the lever that moves the entire network. If you've owned a product where the buyer sets the rules, the daily user is someone else, and trust had to be earned before anything could be automated — we want to talk to you.

If you're not sure you meet every requirement above but believe you could be exceptional here: apply anyway. Seriously.

THE ROLE

You’re a builder: an experienced engineer who wants to understand the customer’s problem, work out a useful solution, and build it yourself. You’re happiest close to customers and hands-on in the code, turning what you learn into software that improves how people work.

Strong engineering is table stakes. Your experience gives you the judgment to make sound technical decisions, move quickly, and take solutions through to production autonomously. You use that independence to focus on customer value.

You’ll work closely with a Product Manager and design to understand problems and shape solutions. You bring your own product judgment, work through the details as you build, and stay accountable for whether the result makes a meaningful difference.



WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Understand the work firsthand. Spend time with estimators, parts managers, appraisers, repairers, and suppliers. Understand their workflows, constraints, and workarounds well enough to distinguish what they ask for from what would make a meaningful difference. This is a core weekly activity.

 - Shape the product with your PM. Bring customer insight, technical understanding, and evidence from what you’ve shipped into decisions about priorities and solutions. Work closely with your PM to challenge assumptions, weigh opportunities, and decide what’s worth building.

 - Build with autonomy. Take a shared understanding of the customer problem through technical design, implementation, and production. Connect the user experience to the underlying systems and make engineering decisions independently. Work with your PM and design when new evidence or trade-offs change the product direction.

 - Move quickly through good judgment. Find the simplest approach that serves the customer. Know when to prototype, when to invest, which compromises are acceptable, and where reliability or correctness must hold. Own the consequences of those decisions.

 - Choose the right way to learn. Use observation, interviews, manual tests, prototypes, or production code according to what you need to find out. Use AI-assisted tools where they help you learn and deliver faster.

 - Follow through on outcomes. Define success with your PM, instrument what you build, and stay accountable for adoption, customer value, and production performance. Reconcile customer feedback with usage data, investigate when they disagree, and change direction when the evidence calls for it.

 - Build trustworthy agentic experiences. Work out where automation genuinely helps, where people need control, and how the experience and underlying systems earn trust in high-stakes workflows. Make the product feel clear, fast, and dependable to the people using it.



MULTIPLY THE TEAM’S IMPACT

Your contribution should make the people and systems around you more effective.

 - Set strong examples. Demonstrate good engineering judgment, customer understanding, and pragmatic delivery in work others can learn from and build on.

 - Build repeatable solutions where they help. Recognise recurring problems and create shared components, tools, or patterns that make future work faster and more reliable. Know when a focused solution is enough and when an abstraction earns its complexity.

 - Coach through real work. Pair with teammates, give thoughtful reviews, and explain the reasoning behind decisions. Help others develop the judgment and confidence to work more independently.

 - Share what you learn. Make useful customer insights, technical lessons, and approaches easy to find and apply across the team.



WHAT YOU BRING


THE ENGINEERING BASELINE

 - Established senior engineering capability. You have substantial experience building and operating production software—typically five or more years—with clear evidence of independent ownership. You can explain the architecture, constraints, failure modes, and trade-offs of technically demanding work you personally delivered. Demonstrated capability matters more than years or previous titles alone.

 - Engineering autonomy and sound judgment. You can take an ambiguous problem through to a production solution without needing engineering direction. You know when to seek specialist input and remain accountable for how the whole solution works.

 - Strong engineering across the product. You can work across the user experience, backend services, and data flows needed to solve the problem. Your depth may vary by area, but you can reason about the system as a whole, make consequential technical decisions, and protect the quality that matters.

 - A track record of moving quickly and responsibly. You simplify scope, use effective tools, and make deliberate technical trade-offs. You can show where that judgment accelerated delivery, what quality you protected, and what happened to the compromises afterwards.


WHAT MAKES YOU RIGHT FOR THIS ROLE

 - Customer and business understanding. You have a habit of spending time with users in their work context and can show how that understanding changed what you built—or whether you built it at all.

 - Ownership of outcomes. You care whether customers use the solution and whether it improves their work. You can connect your decisions to customer value and business results, and you follow through beyond launch.

 - Product judgment and craft. You help decide what should exist, how it should work, and what to leave out. You build experiences that feel clear and dependable to time-pressured, non-technical users.

 - A close, active partnership with your PM. You contribute to product thinking throughout discovery and delivery, bringing your own customer understanding and technical judgment. You can move forward without a detailed specification while keeping your PM involved in consequential product decisions.

 - Comfort with uncertainty. You work with your PM to clarify the problem, then independently work through the unknowns involved in building the solution. You make progress without needing every detail settled upfront.

 - An analytical approach. You can define useful measures with your PM, get the evidence you need, and act on it. You distinguish what the data shows from what you’re assuming.

 - A habit of helping others succeed. You make your reasoning clear, give useful feedback, and leave behind code, tools, and knowledge that others can build on.


PARTICULARLY RELEVANT EXPERIENCE

 - Founder, founding engineer, or early startup work with substantial personal ownership of customer problems and technical delivery. What you owned, learned, and delivered matters more than the company’s eventual size or success.

 - Operational or workflow-heavy B2B products, marketplaces, or systems serving multiple types of user.

 - AI-assisted or agent-driven features in production, especially where human oversight and trust matter.

 - Evidence that you changed or abandoned something you believed in because customer feedback or results showed a better path.

Experience in automotive, repair, parts, or insurance is useful, as is familiarity with Rust, which is part of our stack. Neither is required.

You don’t need every technology or domain experience listed here. The essential requirements are established engineering independence and demonstrated ownership of customer problems and outcomes. If you can show those through an unconventional background, we’d like to hear from you.

Partly is building the infrastructure for anyone to repair anything. We believe everything built should be repairable, and we're building frontier AI to put repair knowledge to work, starting with the $2tn automotive market.

It powers PartlyRepair, used by collision shops, workshops and suppliers to take the admin off the job; PartlyLabs, the agentic infrastructure enterprises use to deploy Interpreter across their own workflows; and a developer API.

Founded by ex-Rocket Lab engineers, we've raised a $50m Series B led by DST Global (Anthropic, Airbnb, Meta, TikTok, Spotify), with Blackbird Ventures, WNDR, Activant Capital, Icehouse Ventures, Square Peg, Airtree and Ecliptic Venture Capital. 🖍️ THIS ROLE

As Partly's first Implementation & Customer Success Manager in the US, you'll found the function that makes shops successful after they sign. You'll own implementation, onboarding and retention for independent collision shops and multi-shop operators (MSOs) with up to 20 locations.

You work hand in hand with Sales. Once a shop says yes, you take it from there: getting Partly installed and connected, training the team, and making Partly part of how they write and source every job. Then you keep them there. You'll be in shops in person, sometimes flying out to do it, speaking the language of owners, estimators and parts managers.

 - Support Sales. Step in before signature when a shop needs a technical walkthrough or proof that it will work in their environment.

 - Be the shop's trusted contact. Be the day-to-day contact for shop owners, estimators and parts managers, and the person they call when something isn't working.

 - Show up in person. Visit shops on site to implement, troubleshoot and build relationships, including regular travel across the US.

 - Resolve issues to ground. Diagnose where a shop is stuck, whether that's installation, the estimating integration or their workflow. Fix what you can yourself and work with Engineering on the rest, rather than just passing tickets on.

 - Bring product thinking to the shop floor. Understand what's really behind a shop's request. Tell the difference between what one shop wants and what most shops need, and back it with what you saw across shops.
